purpose: PRIVATE context evidence only. Published floors, guides, and vendor-authored claims are not quotes for a specified geometry and cannot validate ProofShape estimate accuracy. Quote-locked validation requires the same geometry, quantity, material, finish, location, lead time, and quote date.

entries.vendor_claim: X Resin (SLA): Price from $0.3; tolerance +/-0.2mm or 0.3%; recommended wall >0.8mm; max build 780x780x530mm
entries.notes: Floor price for a tiny sample part. Validates engine small-part AM floor order of magnitude, not any specific geometry.

entries.vendor_claim: TPU (FDM): Price from $3.00; tolerance +/-0.3mm within 100mm; wall 1.6mm (1.2mm min); max build 250x250x250mm
entries.notes: Floor price. FDM TPU minimum wall 1.2mm is well above the engine's 0.8mm generic FDM wall gate - engine gate is for rigid materials; do not cross-apply.

entries.vendor_claim: 316L Stainless Steel (SLM): Price from $8.00; tolerance +/-0.3mm or 0.4%; wall 2.0mm (1.5mm minimum); max build 390x390x290mm; surface Ra 3.2-12um
entries.notes: Metal AM floor roughly 25x the polymer SLA floor at the same vendor - sanity anchor for metal-vs-polymer price ratio in engine output.

entries.vendor: jiga.io (2026 market rate guide, US shops)
entries.vendor_claim: 3-axis mill $35-80/hr; 4-axis $60-125/hr; 5-axis $100-200+/hr; CNC lathe $35-85/hr; Swiss $80-140/hr. Materials: Al 6061 $5-15/kg; stainless $15-25/kg; titanium $30-50/kg; PEEK $100+/kg. Worked example: basic aluminum part $145 @qty1, $55 @qty10, $38 @qty100 (setup $100 amortized).
entries.notes: Rate guide, not a quote. Engine's CNC hourly rate assumptions should sit inside these bands for US shops. Worked example validates setup-amortization curve shape.

entries.vendor_claim: Aluminum molds begin around $1,500, deliver in 7 days or less, good for ~10,000 parts as a rule of thumb. Steel tooling for million-plus volumes exceeds $50,000.
entries.notes: Validates engine IM tooling-tier floor (~$1.5k aluminum prototype tool) and the steel-tool capital band. Engine R3 reference band starts at $1.5-8k for <50mm parts - consistent.

entries.vendor_claim: For quantities of 20+, SLS is the most cost effective additive process. A CNC part quoted at qty 50 lands as much as 70% lower per unit than at qty 1.
entries.notes: Directional, not a price point. Validates the engine's quantity-curve shape: steep unit-cost drop with qty via setup/nesting amortization.

entries.vendor: in-repo R1 reference (public service-bureau bands, stated basis in backend/src/costing/harness.py)
entries.vendor_claim: FDM 0.08-0.60 $/cm3; resin 0.20-1.80 $/cm3; powder-bed (SLS/MJF) 0.25-1.50 $/cm3; handling $3-25/part; bureau order minimums: CNC $75-150, powder-bed $50-100, resin $25-60, FDM $15-35.
entries.notes: Secondary anchor, already in repo. Kept here so the validation set is self-contained. JLC3DP floors above are consistent: $0.3 SLA and $3 FDM sample floors sit under the resin/FDM minimums because they are loss-leader sample prices, not bureau order minimums.

honesty_rules: SOURCE_OBSERVED means the cited page text was retrieved, not that vendor-authored claims were independently confirmed.
Published floors and market guides are context only and never per-geometry accuracy evidence.
Quote-locked accuracy requires the same geometry, quantity, material, finish, location, lead time, and quote date; this set contains none.
No entry may be deleted to improve a result; unavailable or conflicting evidence remains explicit.
